Pre-requisite: Engineering Thermodynamics (MBME04010), Thermal Engineering
(BTME04011), Heat Transfer (BTME06001)
Objectives:
 To provide knowledge of combustion process in I.C Engines.
 To study the various conventional and alternative fuels with their performance on I.C
Engines.
 To provide the knowledge for modern trends in I.C engines, emission standards and
pollution control measures.
Outcomes:
After completion of the course, students would be able to:
 Understand the combustion process in I.C Engines.
 Analyze different electronic fuel injection system, supercharging and its effect on
performance of SI and CI engine.
 Interpret different alternative fuels and its emissions, then the method to control these
emissions.
Detailed Syllabus: (per session plan )
Unit   Description   Duration
1   Types of I. C. Engines: Two stroke four stroke (S.I. and C.I.) engines,   3
engine working principle and valve timing and port timing diagram.
2   Engine performance test: purpose and types, measurement of power,   10
Engine system and performance parameters evaluation, theory of
combustion, principle of combustion, S.I. and C.I. engine combustion
processes and parameters, and its dependence on engine variables.
3   Combustion: adiabatic flame temperature, combustion processes and   10
combustion chambers for SI and CI engines, pollutant formation and
control, effect of engine variables on combustion processes, knocking in
SI and CI engines, petroleum-based fuels, gasoline & diesel fuel and their
properties, blending, knock rating of engine fuels.
4   Carburation: working principles, chemically correct air-fuel ratio and   11
load variation, Carburetors & modern air fuel systems, compensating
devices, venturi and jet dimension calculation, injection system, super
charging, engine lubrication and cooling.

Engines, Alternate fuels like alcohol, hydrogen, natural gas & liquefied
petroleum gas; suitability, engine modifications, merits and demerits as
IC engine fuels.
5   Advances in I.C Engines: Stratified charge spark ignition engine, lean   11
burn engine, dual fuel engine, multi point fuel injection gasoline engine,
homogeneous charge compression ignition engine, plasma ignition,
electric / hybrid vehicles. Pollutant formation and control, emission
standards, pollution monitoring instruments and techniques, control
measures such as DOC, DPF, SCR and LNT.

Outcomes:
After successful completion of the course, students should be able to
 Understand the basics of CFD and working of CFD software and their solution
methodology.
 Analyze the discretized equations for solving heat transfer and fluid flow problems.
 Apply numerical techniques for addressing the problems related to heat transfer,
fluid flow, convection and diffusion.

Unit Description   Duration

predictions like experimental, theoretical working of commercial CFD
software, solution methodology- preprocessing, solver, post processing.

modeling,   Basic   conservation   equation   (continuity   equation,
momentum equation, energy Equation) in differential and Integral form.
Initial and Boundary Conditions, Initial and Boundary Value problems.
One-dimensional computations by Finite Difference, Finite Element and
Finite Volume methods.

unstructured Grids,   O-type, H-type, C-type of Structured Grid
Generation, Mesh Adaptation, The Nature of Numerical Methods, The
Discretization Concept, The Structure of the Discretization Equation,
Methods of Deriving the Discretization Equations, Taylor-Series
Formulation, Variational Formulation, Method of Weighted Residuals,
Control Volume Formulation.

Prerequisite:

The course requires a thorough understanding of Financial Statements - Income Statement,

Balance Sheet and Cash Flow Statement

Objectives:

1. To provide an introduction to essential aspects of Finance Theory and Practice and explain
the financial aspect of various functional decisions.

2. To introduce the basic concept of risk and return.
3. To explain the application of financial tools in security valuation and capital budgeting.

4. To elucidate the application of various models and frameworks to evaluate financing
decisions

Outcomes:

After completion of this course, students should be able to:

1. Take Finance related decisions of a firm

2. Apply the concept of Time Value of Money (TVM); return of projects.

3. Develop the ability to analyse risk and compute the return of projects

4. Design Capital Structure

by creating an innovative and learning organization. It aims to focus on innovation
within business entities, from the technology product or process innovation programs,
to broader perspective addressing innovation as a holistic strategic management
imperative not limited to research & development or New Product Development.

frameworks born out of Creative thinking, Various types of Innovations, Design
Thinking, Process of Innovation, Process of Innovation Management and Developing
Innovation Strategy.

Innovation at an individual level (development of new products & services) as well as
Managing Innovation at an organizational level to get a competitive advantage.

business strategy

Funnel’ - Idea to Execution
